papers.title: Sample, Align, Synthesize: Graph-Based Response Synthesis with ConGrs
papers.authors: S. Ghosh, S.S. Warraich, D. Tarsadiya, G. Yauney, S. Swayamdipta
papers.description: Developed and validated a consensus decoding framework applied to factuality-critical tasks (long-form biography generation and PopQA), establishing robust baselines and characterizing the factuality-information tradeoff.
highlights: Conducted systematic evaluations across long-form biography generation and PopQA benchmarks with **5 independent replications per model**, establishing robust baseline performance metrics
Designed and implemented **high-throughput batch processing infrastructure** for FActScore evaluation, engineering response caching that resolved critical processing bottlenecks
Architected comprehensive **ablation studies** on sample-size scaling during alignment and response synthesis, plus temperature-based sensitivity analysis
Extended the framework to **refusal-aware settings** across Numerical False Presuppositions, Scientific Attributions, and Historical Events, integrating LLM-as-a-judge abstention detection

papers.title: How Reliable is Language Model Micro-Benchmarking?
papers.authors: G. Yauney, S.S. Warraich, S. Swayamdipta
papers.description: Proposed a confidence-based stratified sampling methodology for micro-benchmark selection in LLM meta-evaluation, adapting principled statistical techniques from computer vision literature.
highlights: Designed **confidence-based stratified sampling** for micro-benchmark selection, adapting techniques from computer vision literature to language model evaluation
Built comprehensive evaluation infrastructure integrating **stratified sampling, TinyBenchmarks (P-IRT, GP-IRT), and task-reduction baselines** for systematic comparison
Maintained and extended a modular, reproducible research codebase for meta-evaluation experiments across benchmark selection methodologies

items.title: ConGrs: Graph-Based Response Synthesis for Factual LLM Generation
items.description: A consensus decoding framework validated on factuality-critical tasks (long-form biography generation and PopQA), establishing baseline factuality-information tradeoff curves. Accepted to COLM 2026.
items.problem: LLMs trade off factual accuracy for informativeness in long-form generation. Consensus and sampling-based decoding methods hadn't been rigorously validated for factuality-critical tasks like biography generation and open-domain QA.
approach: Applied a consensus decoding framework across long-form biography generation and PopQA, running 5 independent replications per model
Built high-throughput batch FActScore evaluation infrastructure with response caching to resolve processing bottlenecks
Ran ablations on sample-size scaling and temperature sensitivity during alignment and response synthesis
Extended the framework to refusal-aware settings (Numerical False Presuppositions, Scientific Attributions, Historical Events) with LLM-as-a-judge abstention detection
impact: Established baseline factuality-information tradeoff curves for consensus decoding
Resolved evaluation-pipeline bottlenecks in large-scale FActScore batch processing
items.role: Researcher, under Prof. Swabha Swayamdipta, USC

items.title: Reliable Micro-Benchmarking for LLM Evaluation
items.description: A confidence-based stratified sampling framework for cheaper, more reliable LLM micro-benchmark selection, compared systematically against TinyBenchmarks and task-reduction baselines. ICLR 2026 Oral.
items.problem: Full LLM benchmark suites are expensive to run repeatedly, and existing micro-benchmark subsampling methods for meta-evaluation lacked principled reliability guarantees adapted from other fields.
approach: Adapted confidence-based stratified sampling from computer vision literature to language model evaluation
Built evaluation infrastructure comparing stratified sampling against TinyBenchmarks (P-IRT, GP-IRT) and task-reduction baselines
Maintained a modular, reproducible codebase supporting systematic comparison across benchmark selection methodologies
impact: A principled framework for cheaper, more reliable LLM micro-benchmark selection
Accepted to ICLR 2026 as an Oral presentation
